Greeks. To judge of the doctrines by their effects, one would think that this religion were called
the religion of Christ and Charity, ut lucus a non lucendo [‘as the grove is so named from its not
shining’, i.e. by a paradoxical derivation], when I consider the manner in which they seem to have
transformed the disposition and understanding of you and men of the most amiable manners
and the highest accomplishments, so that even when recommending Christianity you cannot
forbear breathing out defiance, against the express words of Christ. (L ii 230)
